images.alt:
Despite the injuries, the Thunder are one of five teams with only two losses. And they’re looking dominant again, having beaten the Grizzlies and Wizards by a total of 70 points over the weekend.

Two takeaways

Over the course of 27 hours, the Thunder climbed from 12th to third on defense. The Grizzlies’ 97 points on 104 possessions on Friday was their worst offensive game of the season, and the Wizards’ 75 on 99 was the worst offensive game for any team by a wide margin. The two teams combined to shoot just 32-for-76 (42%) in the paint.

The Thunder have seen the league’s biggest drop, by a wide margin, in 3-point rate. They’ve taken just 35.5% of their shots from beyond the arc, the league’s second-lowest rate, down from 42.6% (13th highest) last season. But they’ve outscored their opponents in the paint in each of their last nine games. Ajay Mitchell’s 15.6 points in the paint per 36 minutes trail only the marks of Giannis Antetokounmpo and Victor Wembanyama among 287 players who’ve played at least 100 minutes total.

Coming up: The Thunder’s longest road trip of the season is only four games long, and it begins with a Tuesday-Wednesday back-to-back in Portland. They blew a 22-point lead and suffered their first loss of the season at the Moda Center around this time last year.

items.title: “It’s great to be back,” #Magic guard Desmond Bane, who missed Saturday at Golden State due to an illness, told Kendra Douglas and Josh Cohen on Monday. “I don’t like being away from the team, being bunkered down in my room. But I’m feeling better.”
items.author: Jason Beede
items.body_excerpt:
“It’s great to be back,” #Magic guard Desmond Bane, who missed Saturday at Golden State due to an illness, told Kendra Douglas and Josh Cohen on Monday. “I don’t like being away from the team, being bunkered down in my room. But I’m feeling better.”
